figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. Taxane biosynthetic pathway. Unrevealed steps are shown in highlighted in bold red. Geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase (GGPPS), taxadiene synthase 
(TXS), taxadiene-5α-hydroxylase (T5αOH), taxadiene-5α-ol-O-acetyl transferase (TAT), taxane-10β-hydroxylase (T10αH), taxadiene-2α-hydroxylase (T2αOH), tax­
ane-7β-hydroxylase (T7βOH), taxane-13α-hydroxylase (T13αOH), taxane-1β-hydroxylase (T1βOH), taxane-9α-hydroxylase (T9αOH), taxane-2α-O-bezoyl-transferase 
(TBT), 10-deacetylbaccatinIII-10β-O-acetyltransferase (DBAT), baccatin III 13-O-(3-amino,13-phenylpropanoyl) transferase (BAPT), 3′-N-debenzoyl-2′-deoxytaxol-N- 
benzoyltransferase (DBTNBT).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. Sequence alignment of candidate tags (TB224, TB331 and TB574) and characterized hydroxylases of the taxane biosynthetic pathway. A) Consensus sequence 
of AGxDT motif (in yellow). B) Consensus sequence of PERF motif (in orange) C) Consensus sequence of ETLR motif (in blue). D) Consensus sequence of the heme 
binding region, PFGGGxRxCxG (in red).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. Ligands created for molecular docking analysis. The different ligands are named by Lm followed by the respective number. In red are presented the functional 
groups that were alternated to build all feasible combinations.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6. A) Binding energy (BE) and ligand efficiency (LE) values of the ligands (Lm) for the protein TB574. The X indicates the position of the functional groups 
hydroxylated. The BEs are gradient colored depending on their value, being dark green with the lowest energy and dark red with the highest BE energy. Resolution 
indicates the bound distance between the ligand and the heme group of the TB574. The values resolution values (Å) lower than 3.8 Å are colored in green. B) Ligands 
that can be putatively catabolized by the TB574.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 7. The yeast consortium consisting of three strains synthesizing taxadiene-5α-acetoxy-1β,10β-diol (T5αAcO-1β-10β-diol). EJ3 contains pLR48 expressing TAT 
gene, EJ4 contains pLR49 expressing T10βOH and AE1 contains pAE11 expressing T1βOH. The strains were grown in 24-well plates. Inoculation of different ratios of 
the three strains leads to the production of novel T1βOH. The colors represent the corresponding compounds and multiple lines represent multiple reaction steps.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 8. Chromatogram of a consortium of 3 different S. cerevisiae strains. A) GC-MS chromatogram corresponding to the control (without T1βOH). No peak is detected 
after 9.66. B) The GC-MS chromatogram corresponding to the consortium with a 1:1:2 inoculation ratio, the peak corresponding to the new potential compound can 
be seen at 9.76. C) The GC-MS chromatogram corresponding to the consortium with a 1:1:6 inoculation ratio. The peak corresponding to the new potential compound 
can be seen at 9.75.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 9
figure_candidates.caption: Fig. 9. Mass spectrum of the different consortia for the potentially new T1β-diol compound. A) 1:1:2 inoculation ratio B) 1:1:6 inoculation ratio.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 10
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 10. Production of different taxanes by a consortium of 3 different S. cerevisiae strains grown in YP media. The strains used were, EJ3, EJ4 and AE1 and were 
present at 1:1:2 ratio with 1.0:1.0:2.0 initial OD600 and 1:1:6 ratio with 0.125:0.125:0.75 initial OD600 for the first and second consortium respectively. The 
experiment was done in 2% galactose in 24 well plates for 3 days at 30 ◦C degrees at 350 rpm, Error bars represent the standard deviation of the replicates (n = 3 for 
1:1:2 while n = 4 for 1:1:6). The dataset was analyzed for normality using the Shapiro-Wilk test and for homogeneity of variances using the Levene’s test. Sub­
sequently, the Friedman test was conducted to examine the effects of inoculation ratios on the different metabolites. The Mann-Whitney test was used to study the 
significance of changes in individual metabolites. A p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant, with significance levels denoted as * <0.05, ** 
<0.005, and *** <0.001.
